Spot-checked the map's line numbers against the code and they hold: `Dictate.js:1117` `revise_chunk`, `Widget.js:520/526` `refined · $`, `Mic.js:620` `await_clean`, `Servex.js:599` `/api/tidy`, `Servex.js:198-201` assistant start, `Sessions.js:485/499/759/771`, `engine.js:324/336`.

Two "Unknowns" are one grep away and should simply be answered: `ux/Revise/Revise.js:8` posts to `servex_url("/api/tidy")`, and the switch at `Servex.js:273` is `SERVEX_NO_LAYERS`, which turns off Layers, Global and Sessions (and with it the `refined` cost line) — `dictation-refine-connection-map-2026-10-08.md:32,35`.

The headline says the cost is "the clean step", but `Sessions.refine()` sums both `clean()` and `structure()` calls (`Sessions.js:488-499`); the table and the second section say this correctly, so the first paragraph (`dictation-refine-connection-map-2026-10-08.md:3`) should say "clean-and-structure" to match.

The opening sentence implies one clean path, but there can be two: the browser-side `Revise.run` → `/api/tidy` in Dictate/Mic (off by default, `Dictate.js:1218`) and the Servex-side Echo refine. One line saying which one produces the `refined · $x` box and that the browser one writes no cost would remove the ambiguity.

A dated filename (`...-2026-10-08.md`) for what is really the standing reference for this path will read as stale soon; a plain name like `doc/dictation-path.md` with the date inside would age better. Optional.
